newsitem.title: CHINA: China-ruled HK sends home Vietnamese boatpeople.
newsitem.headline: China-ruled HK sends home Vietnamese boatpeople.

text.p: Hong Kong resumed deporting Vietnamese migrants on Thursday, five weeks after the former British colony returned to Chinese rule, the government said.
Thursday's repatriation flight carrying 102 Vietnamese migrants was the first by the China-backed Hong Kong government.
The returnees, commonly called boatpeople because many arrive by sea, included 97 men and five women.
They had been held in a closed camp since arriving here last year, a government statement said.
Some 3,000 boatpeople are held in detention in Hong Kong despite China's repeated call to Britain to clear the detention centres before Beijing took over the territory on July 1.
However, the Beijing government appears to have taken no action on the issue, leaving it to local Hong Kong authorities to continue the repatriation programme as best it can.
Security sources were quoted by newspapers on Thursday as saying the new Hong Kong government is lobbying Hanoi to speed up the process.
The boatpeople drama began almost two decades ago, when tens of thousands of people fled after the 1975 Communist victory in the Vietnam War.
